summary: The neutral default used when the target market is unknown, when applying to several markets at once, or when applying to a remote-first employer with no single hiring country. It favours conventions that are safe across borders.

photo.note: Off by default. Photos are expected in some markets, discouraged in others, and either way they add little to a screening decision. Enable it only if you know the target market wants one.

personalInfo.note: Keep only what a recruiter needs to contact you and to assess fit. Date of birth, marital status and identity numbers are off by default in every market profile.

page.note: Two pages is a safe default almost everywhere. Keep the first page self-sufficient: many reviewers never turn it over.

notes: When a document may be read by an unknown parser, prefer a single column, standard section headings and no graphics.
Dates in MM/YYYY avoid the DD/MM versus MM/DD ambiguity that breaks date parsing in cross-border applications.
Write the CV in the language of the advert or of the employer's working language.
Use one spelling convention consistently: mixing US and UK English in one document reads as carelessness.

advisories.text: For an international application, tailoring the summary and the skills list to the advert has more effect than any formatting choice.
For remote-first employers, stating your working time zone and right to work where relevant saves a screening round.
Where a qualification is not recognised abroad, add a one-line explanation of its level and duration rather than assuming the reader will know it.
